bibl.title: Circular RNAs Are the Predominant Transcript Isoform from Hundreds of Human Genes in Diverse Cell Types

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: human transcripts whose exons appear in an order the genome does not specify - for thirty years an anomaly, here the predominant isoform of hundreds of genes
span.quote: Statistical estimates and biochemical assays provided strong evidence that a substantial fraction of the spliced transcripts from hundreds of genes are circular RNAs. Our results suggest that a non-canonical mode of RNA splicing, resulting in a circular RNA isoform, is a general feature of the gene expression program in human cells.

span.label: whether scrambled-exon transcripts are reverse-transcription artefacts or real circular RNA molecules, and how abundant they are
span.quote: Indeed, it has been recently suggested that apparent examples of exon scrambling in human EST databases are primarily explained as RT artifacts.

span.label: deep sequencing plus a physical assay showing that scrambled-exon transcripts are circular, at levels comparable to the canonical linear mRNA
span.quote: Indeed, for many genes, in both cancer and normal human cells, we found RNAs with circularly permuted exon orders at levels comparable to those of the canonical, linear mRNA.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Statistical estimates and biochemical assays provided strong evidence that a substantial fraction of the spliced transcripts from hundreds of genes are circular RNAs. Our results suggest that a non-canonical mode of RNA splicing, resulting in a circular RNA isoform, is a general feature of the gene expression program in human cells.

span.label: non-canonical splicing joining a donor to an UPSTREAM acceptor, producing a closed circular RNA that survives exonuclease
span.quote: transcripts with scrambled exons were generally resistant to RNaseR treatment, as expected for circular RNAs, but not for RNAs with scrambled exons generated by template switching or other artifacts of reverse transcription from a canonical linear RNA.

span.label: paired-end RNA-Seq of normal and malignant human cells, statistical abundance estimation, and RNase R digestion as the discriminating biochemical assay
span.term: paired-end RNA-Seq of normal and malignant human cells, statistical abundance estimation, and RNase R digestion as the discriminating biochemical assay
span.quote: transcripts with scrambled exons were generally resistant to RNaseR treatment, as expected for circular RNAs, but not for RNAs with scrambled exons generated by template switching or other artifacts of reverse transcription from a canonical linear RNA.

span.label: RNase R digests linear RNA and not covalently closed circles, so ONE TREATMENT SEPARATES THE TWO HYPOTHESES: circles survive, and template-switching artefacts of a linear molecule would not
span.quote: transcripts with scrambled exons were generally resistant to RNaseR treatment, as expected for circular RNAs, but not for RNAs with scrambled exons generated by template switching or other artifacts of reverse transcription from a canonical linear RNA.

span.label: circular RNAs lack a poly-A tail, so they are enriched in the non-poly-adenylated fraction - a second, independent physical property pointing the same way
span.quote: In an analysis of publicly available RNA-Seq data from HeLa and H9 human embryonic stem cells, we found that RNAs with scrambled exons were enriched in non-poly-adenylated fractions.

span.label: THE PAPER NAMES THE DIRECTION OF ITS OWN ERROR AND IT POINTS AGAINST ITS OWN CLAIM'S SIZE: `the limitations of our experimental design MAY ACTUALLY HAVE LED US TO UNDERESTIMATE the prevalence of circular RNA isoforms`
span.quote: While we have found that hundreds of human genes express circular RNA isoforms, the limitations of our experimental design may actually have led us to underestimate the prevalence of circular RNA isoforms.

span.label: the first route to that under-count is the size-selection step, which would miss small circular RNAs and highly structured ones whose fragmentation kinetics do not suit the selection
span.quote: First, the size selection step during sequencing library preparation would miss small circular RNAs, or highly structured circular RNAs with fragmentation kinetics incompatible with our size selection.

span.label: and the second is the counting method itself: a circular transcript also yields read pairs in the canonical linear orientation, so those reads are credited to the linear isoform
span.quote: Note that assuming sequencing reads are sampled uniformly across each transcript, this method underestimates the total fraction of transcripts containing exons in scrambled order, as scrambled transcripts are also expected to yield read pairs corresponding to the canonical linear orientation.

span.label: the prior literature it must overturn is itself confounded - EST database studies are `fraught with confounding of RT-PCR artifacts and selection bias`, so the negative evidence was never clean either
span.quote: The lack of direct experimental evidence makes interpretation of these studies difficult: EST database studies are fraught with confounding of RT-PCR artifacts and selection bias.

span.label: RNase R digestion is applied to canonical linear transcripts AND to scrambled-exon transcripts in the same experiment
span.note: eliminates: the reverse-transcription artefact hypothesis specifically - a linear molecule mis-copied during RT would be digested, and a covalently closed circle would not. ONE TREATMENT, TWO PREDICTIONS, AND THEY DIFFER · outcome: held
span.quote: transcripts with scrambled exons were generally resistant to RNaseR treatment, as expected for circular RNAs, but not for RNAs with scrambled exons generated by template switching or other artifacts of reverse transcription from a canonical linear RNA.

span.label: the poly-adenylated and non-poly-adenylated fractions are compared in independent public data from HeLa and H9 cells
span.note: eliminates: a result that depends on this laboratory's library preparation - and it uses somebody else's data to do it · outcome: held
span.quote: In an analysis of publicly available RNA-Seq data from HeLa and H9 human embryonic stem cells, we found that RNAs with scrambled exons were enriched in non-poly-adenylated fractions.

span.label: the artefact hypothesis is given a QUANTITATIVE prediction before being tested - 1 in 22,500 template switches at an exon boundary, hundreds expected in an EST database
span.note: eliminates: a rival explanation dismissed by assertion; here it is stated in a form that could have won · outcome: held
span.quote: If template switching occurs during reverse transcription, given a typical human exon length of 150 (the average of the lower 90th quantile), 1 out of 22500 template switches would be at exon-exon boundaries, and hundreds could be expected to be detected in an EST database.

span.label: whether the abundance estimate is an upper or a lower bound
span.note: eliminates: an inflated headline - the paper argues the number is TOO LOW, by two named routes, while the number is what makes the paper interesting · outcome: held
span.quote: While we have found that hundreds of human genes express circular RNA isoforms, the limitations of our experimental design may actually have led us to underestimate the prevalence of circular RNA isoforms.

span.label: exon-scrambling
span.quote: These scrambled transcripts were estimated to comprise less than one one-thousandth of DCC transcripts, and the phenomenon was dubbed exon-scrambling

span.label: circular RNAs
span.quote: First, the size selection step during sequencing library preparation would miss small circular RNAs, or highly structured circular RNAs with fragmentation kinetics incompatible with our size selection.

span.label: template switching
span.quote: transcripts with scrambled exons were generally resistant to RNaseR treatment, as expected for circular RNAs, but not for RNAs with scrambled exons generated by template switching or other artifacts of reverse transcription from a canonical linear RNA.

span.label: RNaseR
span.quote: transcripts with scrambled exons were generally resistant to RNaseR treatment, as expected for circular RNAs, but not for RNAs with scrambled exons generated by template switching or other artifacts of reverse transcription from a canonical linear RNA.

span.label: exon-scrambling - THE NAME THE PHENOMENON CARRIED FOR THIRTY YEARS, and the name is the verdict: a scramble is a mistake. Estimated at LESS THAN ONE ONE-THOUSANDTH of a gene's transcripts and widely explained as reverse-transcription artefact. This paper renames the same observation `circular RNA isoform` and puts it in the title as PREDOMINANT
span.quote: These scrambled transcripts were estimated to comprise less than one one-thousandth of DCC transcripts, and the phenomenon was dubbed exon-scrambling

span.label: circular RNA - AS ESTABLISHED HERE, BY EXONUCLEASE RESISTANCE rather than by sequence. The sequence evidence is the same evidence the artefact hypothesis uses; what separates them is a physical property of the molecule, and that is why the RNase R sentence is the paper
span.quote: transcripts with scrambled exons were generally resistant to RNaseR treatment, as expected for circular RNAs, but not for RNAs with scrambled exons generated by template switching or other artifacts of reverse transcription from a canonical linear RNA.

span.label: the artefact hypothesis - STATED WITH ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN DISMISSED: at a typical exon length of 150, 1 in 22,500 template switches lands on an exon boundary, and hundreds would therefore appear in an EST database. The rival explanation is given its own quantitative prediction before being tested against one
span.quote: If template switching occurs during reverse transcription, given a typical human exon length of 150 (the average of the lower 90th quantile), 1 out of 22500 template switches would be at exon-exon boundaries, and hundreds could be expected to be detected in an EST database.

span.label: how it was found - `Although our INITIAL GOAL was to discover cancer-specific chromosomal rearrangements`, and `WE WERE SURPRISED TO FIND` the permuted orders. The finding is a by-product of a search for something else, and the paper says so rather than reconstructing a hypothesis it did not have
span.quote: Although our initial goal was to discover cancer-specific chromosomal rearrangements by identifying the resulting fused or rearranged transcripts, we also investigated the possibility that the exon order specified by the genome sequence might be rearranged during RNA processing.

span.label: critiques → the explanation of scrambled exons as reverse-transcription artefacts, which RNase R resistance and non-poly-adenylation both contradict
span.quote: Taken together, these findings provide strong evidence that most scrambled exon sequences we detected in human RNA were derived from circular molecules.

span.label: critiques → the EST-database literature on exon scrambling, as confounded by RT-PCR artefacts and selection bias in both directions
span.quote: The lack of direct experimental evidence makes interpretation of these studies difficult: EST database studies are fraught with confounding of RT-PCR artifacts and selection bias.

span.label: contradicts → the estimate that scrambled transcripts comprise less than one one-thousandth of a gene's output - here they are comparable to the canonical linear mRNA
span.quote: Indeed, for many genes, in both cancer and normal human cells, we found RNAs with circularly permuted exon orders at levels comparable to those of the canonical, linear mRNA.

span.label: A CLASS OF MOLECULE SPENT THIRTY YEARS INSIDE THE ERROR TERM: scrambled transcripts were estimated at less than one one-thousandth and the phenomenon was DUBBED EXON-SCRAMBLING - a name that is itself the verdict
span.term: A CLASS OF MOLECULE SPENT THIRTY YEARS INSIDE THE ERROR TERM: scrambled transcripts were estimated at less than one one-thousandth and the phenomenon was DUBBED EXON-SCRAMBLING - a name that is itself the verdict
span.quote: These scrambled transcripts were estimated to comprise less than one one-thousandth of DCC transcripts, and the phenomenon was dubbed exon-scrambling

span.label: for many genes, in both cancer and normal cells, circularly permuted exon orders occur AT LEVELS COMPARABLE TO the canonical linear mRNA
span.term: for many genes, in both cancer and normal cells, circularly permuted exon orders occur AT LEVELS COMPARABLE TO the canonical linear mRNA
span.quote: Indeed, for many genes, in both cancer and normal human cells, we found RNAs with circularly permuted exon orders at levels comparable to those of the canonical, linear mRNA.

span.label: THE ASSAY THAT SETTLES IT IS PHYSICAL, NOT STATISTICAL: scrambled transcripts resist RNase R as circles would and as template-switching artefacts would not
span.term: THE ASSAY THAT SETTLES IT IS PHYSICAL, NOT STATISTICAL: scrambled transcripts resist RNase R as circles would and as template-switching artefacts would not
span.quote: transcripts with scrambled exons were generally resistant to RNaseR treatment, as expected for circular RNAs, but not for RNAs with scrambled exons generated by template switching or other artifacts of reverse transcription from a canonical linear RNA.

span.label: the artefact hypothesis is given its own arithmetic - 1 in 22,500 template switches at an exon boundary, hundreds expected in an EST database - before being tested
span.term: the artefact hypothesis is given its own arithmetic - 1 in 22,500 template switches at an exon boundary, hundreds expected in an EST database - before being tested
span.quote: If template switching occurs during reverse transcription, given a typical human exon length of 150 (the average of the lower 90th quantile), 1 out of 22500 template switches would be at exon-exon boundaries, and hundreds could be expected to be detected in an EST database.

span.label: THE PAPER ARGUES ITS OWN HEADLINE NUMBER IS TOO LOW, by two named routes: size selection misses small circles, and a circular transcript also yields reads in the canonical linear orientation
span.term: THE PAPER ARGUES ITS OWN HEADLINE NUMBER IS TOO LOW, by two named routes: size selection misses small circles, and a circular transcript also yields reads in the canonical linear orientation
span.quote: While we have found that hundreds of human genes express circular RNA isoforms, the limitations of our experimental design may actually have led us to underestimate the prevalence of circular RNA isoforms.

span.label: the finding is a by-product of a search for something else - the initial goal was cancer-specific chromosomal rearrangements, and `we were SURPRISED to find` the permuted orders
span.term: the finding is a by-product of a search for something else - the initial goal was cancer-specific chromosomal rearrangements, and `we were SURPRISED to find` the permuted orders
span.quote: Although our initial goal was to discover cancer-specific chromosomal rearrangements by identifying the resulting fused or rearranged transcripts, we also investigated the possibility that the exon order specified by the genome sequence might be rearranged during RNA processing.

span.label: the name given to transcripts with exons spliced in non-canonical order, estimated at less than one one-thousandth of DCC transcripts
span.quote: These scrambled transcripts were estimated to comprise less than one one-thousandth of DCC transcripts, and the phenomenon was dubbed exon-scrambling

span.label: template switches, of which 1 would fall at an exon-exon boundary at a typical human exon length of 150 - the artefact hypothesis's own prediction
span.quote: If template switching occurs during reverse transcription, given a typical human exon length of 150 (the average of the lower 90th quantile), 1 out of 22500 template switches would be at exon-exon boundaries, and hundreds could be expected to be detected in an EST database.

span.label: Statistical estimates
span.quote: Statistical estimates and biochemical assays provided strong evidence that a substantial fraction of the spliced transcripts from hundreds of genes are circular RNAs. Our results suggest that a non-canonical mode of RNA splicing, resulting in a circular RNA isoform, is a general feature of the gene expression program in human cells.

span.label: exon order
span.quote: We were surprised to find numerous examples of transcripts in which the exon order was a circular permutation of the order encoded in the genome.
